acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Chaunte Vaughn’s mother recently died of Parkinsons. Even though Chaunte doesn't believe in ghosts, she is visited by her mom's ghost multiple times. And, to Chaunte’s disappointment, everything her mother's ghost has to say seems pointless.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Reporter Chenjerai Kumanyika visits Savannah, Georgia to learn about the city’s popular ghost tours. He’s heard the tourist attractions actually include the brutal reality of slavery. What he finds is more sinister and complex than advertised.
acts.credits: By Chenjerai Kumanyika; Produced by Elna Baker, Valerie Kipnis, Esther Blessing, and George Dawes Greene
acts.title: Ghost Industrial Complex

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Abby Stein’s youngest sister got married last month, the last of 13 kids in their family. At the wedding, an uninvited guest showed up.
acts.title: Wedding Crasher

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc:
In the 1920s, at the height of the Spiritualism movement, a friendship blossomed between two men with opposing views on the topic: Harry Houdini and Sir Arthur Conan Doyle. Houdini was a skeptic. Conan Doyle was the de facto leader of the movement. On a vacation in Atlantic City, the famous author tried to help his skeptical friend talk to the ghost of his beloved mother. Sean Cole reports.
You can read more about Houdini's crusade against the Spiritualism movement in David Jaher's book The Witch of Lime Street.

songs.t: There’s A Ghost in My House
